sanskrit: āgniṁ na svavṛktibhir hotāraṁ tvā vṛṇīmahe | yajñāya stīrṇabarhiṣe vi vo made śīram pāvakaśociṣaṁ vivakṣase ||
english: With our own songs of praise we choose thee, Agni, as Hotṛ for the sacrifice spread with sacred grass. In the exhilaration of your Soma, radiant and pure-flaming, thou art eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: tvām u te svābhuvaḥ śumbhanty aśvarādhasaḥ | veti tvām upasecanī vi vo mada ṛjītir agna āhutir vivakṣase ||
english: Thee, verily, do thy own devotees adorn—those rich in horses. The oblation-ladle seeks thee, O Agni; in the Soma's rapture the forceful offering seeks thee, and thou art eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: tve dharmāṇa āsate juhūbhiḥ siñcatīr iva | kṛṣṇā rūpāṇy arjunā vi vo made viśvā adhi śriyo dhiṣe vivakṣase ||
english: In thee the ordinances rest, like ones pouring with their ladles. Dark forms and bright forms—in the Soma's rapture thou assumest all splendours, and thou art eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: yam agne manyase rayiṁ sahasāvann amartya | tam ā no vājasātaye vi vo made yajñeṣu citram ā bharā vivakṣase ||
english: Whatever wealth thou, O Agni, mighty one, immortal, thinkest of—bring that wondrous treasure to us at the sacrifices for the winning of strength. In the Soma's rapture thou art eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: agnir jāto atharvaṇā vidad viśvāni kāvyā | bhuvad dūto vivrasvato vi vo made priyo yamasya kāmyo vivakṣase ||
english: Agni was born through Atharvan and found all the inspired poems. He became the messenger of Vivasvat—beloved of Yama, the desirable one—in the Soma's exhilaration eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: tvāṁ yajñeṣv īḻate 'gne pratyaty adhvare | tvaṁ vasūni kāmyā vi vo made viśvā dadhāsi dāśuṣe vivakṣase ||
english: Thee, O Agni, they praise at sacrifices performed in order at the rite. Thou grantest all desirable treasures to the worshipper—in the Soma's rapture eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: tvāṁ yajñeṣv ṛtvijam cārum agne ni ṣedire | ghṛtapratīkam manuṣo vi vo made śukraṁ cetiṣṭham akṣabhir vivakṣase ||
english: Thee, as the beautiful sacrificial priest, O Agni, they have set in the ritual—the bright-faced one of Manu. Most brilliant and most watchful with thine eyes—in the Soma's rapture eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: agne śukreṇa śociṣoru prathayase bṛhat | abhikrandan vṛṣāyase vi vo made garbhaṁ dadhāsi jāmiṣu vivakṣase ||
english: O Agni, with thy bright flame thou spreadest wide and mightily. Roaring like a bull thou art exuberant; in the Soma's rapture thou layest seed in kindred women, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: kuha śruta indraḥ kasmin adya jane mitro na śrūyate | ṛṣīṇāṁ vā yaḥ kṣaye guhā vā carkṛṣe girā ||
english: Where is famed Indra heard? Among which people today is he known, like Mitra? Whether it is in the dwelling of seers, or in a hidden place, where hast thou laboured with thy hymn?

sanskrit: iha śruta indro asme adya stave vajry ṛcīṣamaḥ | mitro na yo janeṣv ā yaśaś cakre asāmy ā ||
english: Here, renowned among us, shall Indra be praised today—the wielder of the vajra, who consumes the sacrificial food; who, like Mitra, has spread his fame unceasingly among peoples.

sanskrit: maho yas patiḥ śavaso asāmy ā maho nṛmṇasya tūtujiḥ | bhartā vajrasya dhṛṣṇoḥ pitā putram iva priyam ||
english: He who is lord of great, unceasing strength, who multiplies great manly power—the bearer of the bold vajra, who cherishes (his devotees) as a father a dear son.

sanskrit: yujāno aśvā vātasya dhunī devo devasya vajrivaḥ | syantā pathā virukmatā sṛjānaḥ stoṣy adhvanaḥ ||
english: Harnessing the swift horses of the wind, O divine Vajra-wielder, releasing them along the shining path, urging them onward—thou art to be praised on the way.

sanskrit: tvaṁ tyā cid vātasyāśvāgā ṛjrā tmanā vahadhyai | yayor devo na martyo yantā nakir vidāyyaḥ ||
english: Thou comest with those swift horses of the wind, which carry thee onward of their own accord—horses whose charioteer no god or mortal, no one at all, can discern.

sanskrit: adha gmantośanā pṛcchate vāṁ kadarthā na ā gṛham | ā jagmathuḥ parākād divaś ca gmaś ca martyam ||
english: And then, going forth, Uśanā asks you two: 'For what purpose do you not come home?' You have come from afar—from heaven and from earth—to the mortal.

sanskrit: ā na indra pṛkṣase asmākam brahmodgatam | tat tvā yācāmhe avaḥ śuṣṇaṁ yad dhann amānuṣam ||
english: Come, O Indra, to taste our uplifted hymn. This we implore of thee—that thou hadst smitten the non-human Śuṣṇa.

sanskrit: akarmā dasyu r abhi no amantur anyavrato amānuṣaḥ | tvaṁ tasyāmitrahan vadhar dāsasya dambhaya ||
english: The Dasyu is without rites, without mind, of alien vows, non-human, who assails us. O slayer of enemies, strike down the weapon of that Dāsa with a crushing blow.

sanskrit: tvaṁ na indra śūra śūrair uta tvotāso barhaṇā | purutrā te vi pūrtayo navanta kṣoṇayo yathā ||
english: Thou, O Indra the hero, with heroes, and those upheld by thee with strength—in many places thy gifts are glorified as the earth-regions rejoice.

sanskrit: tvaṁ tān vṛtrathatye codayo nṝn kārpāṇe śūra vajrivaḥ | guhā yadī kavīnāṁ viśāṁ nakṣatraśavasām ||
english: Thou, O hero Vajra-bearer, hast incited those men to battle against Vṛtra—in the hidden realm of the inspired seers, of the star-empowered peoples.

sanskrit: makṣū tā ta indra dānāpnasa ākṣāṇe śūra vajrivaḥ | yad dha śuṣṇasya dambhayo jātaṁ viśvaṁ sayāvabhiḥ ||
english: Swift are thy gifts, O Indra; they who seize them are fittingly enjoyers, O hero Vajra-bearer—all that thou didst crush of Śuṣṇa's creation with thy companions.

sanskrit: māku dhrya g indra śūra vasvīr asme bhūvann abhiṣṭayaḥ | vayaṁ-vayaṁ ta āsāṁ sumnne syāma vajrivaḥ ||
english: May they not wander away, O Indra, hero—let good succours be ours! May we, we ourselves, dwell in their protection and in thy grace, O Vajra-bearer.

sanskrit: asme tā ta indra santu satyāhiṁsantīr upaspṛśaḥ | vidyāma yāsām bhujo dhenūnāṁ na vajrivaḥ ||
english: May those truly unharmful (cows) of thine be ours, O Indra, with their touch. May we know the enjoyment of those milk-cows, O Vajra-bearer.

sanskrit: ahastā yad apadī vardha ta kṣāḥ śacībhir vedyānām | śuṣṇaṁ pari pradakṣiṇid viśvāyave ni śiśnathaḥ ||
english: When the handless, footless earth swelled up through the deeds of those worthy of knowledge—thou didst strike down Śuṣṇa in a rightward circuit, for the sake of all living beings.

sanskrit: pibā-pibed indra śūra somam mā riṣaṇyo vasavāna vasu ḥ san | uta trāyasva gṛṇato maghoono mahaś ca rāyo revatas kṛdhī naḥ ||
english: Drink, drink, O Indra hero, the Soma—may it not harm thee, thou who possessest wealth, full of riches! And protect the liberal worshipper who sings thy praise, and grant us great and glorious wealth.

sanskrit: yajāmaha indraṁ vajradakṣiṇaṁ harīṇāṁ rathyam vivratānām | pra śmaśru dodhuvad ūrdhvathā bhūd vi senābhir dayamāno vi rādhasā ||
english: We worship Indra who holds the vajra in his right hand, the charioteer of the bay steeds—those that take varied courses. He who shook his beard upward, who distributes bounty, parting (the foe) with his armies, with his gifts.

sanskrit: harī nv asya yā vane vide vasv indro maghair maghavā vṛtrahā bhuvat | ṛbhur vāja ṛbhukṣāḥ patyate śavo 'va kṣṇaumi dāsasya nāma cit ||
english: His two bay horses, found in the forest as wealth—may Indra the bountiful, slayer of Vṛtra, be rich in gifts! Ṛbhu, Vāja, Ṛbhukṣan—he masters strength; I even diminish the very name of the Dāsa.

sanskrit: yadā vajraṁ hiraṇyam id athā rathaṁ harī yam asya vahato vi sūribhiḥ | ā tiṣṭhati maghavā sanaśruta indro vājasya dīrghaśravasas patiḥ ||
english: When he holds his golden vajra, then the bountiful, long-renowned Indra mounts the chariot drawn by those bay horses through (the realms of) the pious—Indra, lord of food and far-famed spoil.

sanskrit: so cin nu vṛṣṭir yūthyā svā sacāṁ indraḥ śmaśrūṇi haritā bhi pruṣṇute | ava veti sukṣayaṁ sute madhūd id dhūnoti vāto yathā vanam ||
english: So indeed is this rain of his own herd—Indra bedews his golden beard; he comes down to the fair dwelling, and at the pressed Soma he shakes (all things) like the wind shaking a forest.

sanskrit: yo vācā vivāco mṛdhravācaḥ purū sahasrāśivā jaghāna | tat-tad id asya pauṁsyaṁ gṛṇīmasi piteva yas taviṣīṁ vāvṛdhe śavaḥ ||
english: He who with his voice out-spoke the hostile voices, who slew many thousands of ill-fortuned foes—these several acts of his manly strength do we proclaim, he who has increased his might as a father (the strength of) a son.

sanskrit: stomaṁ ta indra vimadā ajījanann apūrvyam purutamaṁ sudānave | vidmā hy asya bhojanam inasya yad ā paśuṁ na gopāḥ karāmahe ||
english: Vimada and his companions generated for thee, O Indra, this unprecedented and manifold hymn of praise for the great giver. For we know the feast of this mighty one—what offering we shall make as herdsmen bring the cattle.

sanskrit: mākir na enā sakhyā vi yauṣus tava cendra vimadasyha ca ṛṣeḥ | vidmā hi te pramatiṁ deva jāmivad asme te santu sakhyā śivāni ||
english: May none sever these friendships of thine and ours, O Indra, and of the seer Vimada! For we know thy fore-thought, O god, as one knows a kinsman—may thy friendships with us be gracious.

sanskrit: indra somam imam piba madhumantaṁ camū sutam | asme rayiṁ ni dhāraya vi vo made sahasriṇam purūvaso vivakṣase ||
english: O Indra, drink this honey-sweet Soma pressed in the cup. Bestow upon us thousandfold wealth—in the exhilaration of the Soma-draught, O thou of many gifts, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: tvāṁ yajñebhir ukthair upa havyebhir īmahe | śacīpate śacīnāṁ vi vo made śreṣṭhaṁ no dhehi vāryaṁ vivakṣase ||
english: Thee we approach with sacrifices, hymns, and oblations, O lord of power—lord of mighty deeds. Bestow on us the choicest gift—in the Soma's rapture eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: yas patir vāryāṇām asi raddhrasya coditā | indra stotṝṇām avitā vi vo made dviṣo naḥ pāhy aṁhaso vivakṣase ||
english: Thou who art lord of desirable things, the inciter of the feeble—O Indra, protector of praisers—in the Soma's rapture guard us from adversaries and from distress, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ śakrā māyāvinā samīcī nir amanthatam | vimadena yad īḻitā nāsatyā niramanthatam ||
english: You two mighty ones, possessed of māyā—the Aśvins—rubbed out the fire together; when praised by Vimada, the Nāsatyas rubbed it out (from the kindling-sticks).

sanskrit: viśve devā akṛpanta samīcyor niṣpatantyoḥ | nāsatyāv abruvan devāḥ punar ā vahātād iti ||
english: All the gods mourned as the Aśvins' wives departed. The gods said to the Nāsatyas: 'Bring them back again!'

sanskrit: madhumanme parāyaṇaṁ madhumat punar āyanam | tā no devā devatayā yuvam madhumatas kṛtam ||
english: Honey-sweet be my going forth, honey-sweet my return. O gods, through divine grace make that (journey) sweet for us—you two (Aśvins).

sanskrit: bhadraṁ no api vātaya mano dakṣam uta kratum | adhā te sakhye andhaso vi vo made raṇan gāvo na yavase vivakṣase ||
english: Breathe into us an auspicious mind, O Soma, skill and understanding. So then, in friendship with thee, through thy Soma-draught, in the rapture of the juice, may our prayers resound like cows in the pasture, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: hṛdisṛśas ta āsate viśveṣu soma dhāmasu | adhā kāmā ime mama vi vo made vi tiṣṭhante vasūyavo vivakṣase ||
english: Thy heart-touching (inspirations), O Soma, rest in all thy dwellings. And then my desires—in the Soma's rapture they spread wide, seeking riches, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: uta vratāni soma te prāham mināmi pākyā | adhā piteva sūnave vi vo made mṛḻā no abhi cid vadhād vivakṣase ||
english: And thy ordinances, O Soma, I do not transgress in foolishness. Then, as a father to a son—in the Soma's rapture be gracious to us even against the weapon (of death), eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: sam u pra yanti dhītayaḥ sargāso avatāṁ iva | kratuṁ naḥ soma jīvase vi vo made dhārayā camasāṁ iva vivakṣase ||
english: Together do the inspired thoughts advance, like streams into the lowlands. O Soma, sustain our power of action for life—in the Soma's rapture, holding them up like the cups, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: tava tye soma śaktibhir nikāmāso vy ṛṇvire | gṛtasya dhīrās tavaso vi vo made vrajaṁ gomantam aśvinaṁ vivakṣase ||
english: With thy powers, O Soma, those who desire thee have opened (the enclosures). The wise of the Gṛtsa clan, (endowed) with thy strength—in the Soma's rapture (they win) a cow-filled and horse-filled pen, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: paśuṁ naḥ soma rakṣasi purutrā viṣṭhitaṁ jagat | samākṛṇoṣi jīvase vi vo made viśvā sampaśyan bhuvanā vivakṣase ||
english: Thou guardest our cattle, O Soma, the moving world spread in many places. Thou bringest together for life—in the Soma's rapture, beholding all beings, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: tvaṁ naḥ soma viśvato gopā adābhyo bhava | sedha rājann apa sridho vi vo made mā no duḥśaṁsa īśatā vivakṣase ||
english: Be thou our all-round guardian, O Soma, inviolable king. Drive away all blemishes—in the Soma's rapture, O king, let no slanderer have power over us, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: tvaṁ naḥ soma sukratur vayodheyāya jāgṛhi | kṣetravittaro manuṣo vi vo made draho naḥ pāhy aṁhaso vivakṣase ||
english: Thou, O Soma of good purpose, watch over us for the bestowal of strength. Knowing the field better than Manu—in the Soma's rapture guard us from treachery and distress, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: tvaṁ no vṛtrahantamendra syendo śivaḥ sakhā | yat sīṁ havante samithe vi vo made yudhyamānās tokasātau vivakṣase ||
english: Be thou, O Indu, greatest slayer of Vṛtra, a gracious friend to us—when men invoke thee in battle—in the Soma's rapture, as they fight for the gaining of offspring, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: ayaṁ gha sa turo mada indrasya vardhata priyaḥ | ayaṁ kakṣīvato maho vi vo made matiṁ viprasya vardhayad vivakṣase ||
english: This swift intoxication grows dear to Indra. This great (Soma) increases the inspired thought of Kakṣīvat the seer—in the Soma's rapture eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: ayaṁ viprāya dāśuṣe vājām̐ iyarti gomataḥ | ayaṁ saptabhya ā varaṁ vi vo made prāndhaṁ śroṇaṁ ca tāriṣad vivakṣase ||
english: This Soma sends forth cattle-rich prizes for the inspired worshipper. This (Soma) wins the choicest gift for seven (sages)—in the Soma's rapture it saves both the blind man and the lame, eager to speak forth.

sanskrit: pra hy acchā manīṣāḥ spārhā yanti niyutaḥ | pra dasrā niyudrathaḥ pūṣā aviṣṭu māhinaḥ ||
english: Forward, indeed, go the longed-for prayers toward the Niyuts. Forward—may Pūṣan of the Niyut-chariot, the wondrous, the great one, help (us)!

sanskrit: yasya tyan mahitvaṁ vātāpyam ayaṁ janaḥ | vipra ā vaṁsad dhītibhiś ciketa suṣṭutīnām ||
english: Whose great power coming from the wind this people (praises)—may the inspired poet win him through (his) thoughts; he is known for excellent hymns.

sanskrit: sa veda suṣṭutīnām indur na pūṣā vṛṣā | abhi psuraḥ pruṣāyati vrajaṁ na ā pruṣāyati ||
english: He knows excellent praises—Pūṣan the bull, like the Soma-drop; he sprinkles the eager one; like the pen (full of cattle) he sprinkles (gifts).

sanskrit: maṁsīmahi tvā vayam asmākaṁ deva pūṣan | matīnāṁ ca sādhanaṁ viprāṇāṁ cādhavam ||
english: We shall honour thee, O god Pūṣan, as ours—for the perfecting of (our) thoughts and as the incessant helper of inspired seers.

sanskrit: pratyardhir yajñānām aśvahayo rathānām | ṛṣiḥ sa yo manurhito viprasya yāvayatsakhaḥ ||
english: He is the counterpart of sacrifices, the impeller of horse-drawn chariots. He is the seer set in place by Manu, the companion who drives away (evil) from the inspired poet.

sanskrit: ādhīṣamāṇāyāḥ patiḥ śucāyāś ca śucasya ca | vāsovāyo 'vīnām ā vāsāṁsi marmṛjat ||
english: He is the lord of her who is anxious and of the bright one and of brightness—the weaver of garments; he cleansed the garments of sheep.

sanskrit: ino vājānāṁ patir inaḥ puṣṭīnāṁ sakhā | pra śmaśru haryato dūdhod vi vṛthā yo adābhyaḥ ||
english: He is the mighty one, lord of prizes, the mighty companion of abundance. He who is golden-bright shook out his beard freely—he who is inviolable.

sanskrit: ā te rathasya pūṣann ajā dhuraṁ vavṛtyuḥ | viśvasyārthinaḥ sakhā sanojā anapacyutaḥ ||
english: The goats have turned to the yoke of thy chariot, O Pūṣan—the companion of everyone who seeks, born long ago, never displaced.

sanskrit: asmākam ūrjā ratham pūṣā aviṣṭu māhinaḥ | bhuvad vājānāṁ vṛdha imaṁ naḥ śṛṇavad dhavam ||
english: May Pūṣan the great one help our chariot with his strength. May he increase our prizes and hear this our invocation.

sanskrit: asat su me jaritaḥ sābhivego yat sunvate yajamānāya śikṣam | anāśīrdām aham asmi prahantā satyadhvṛtaṁ vṛjināyantam ābhum ||
english: Let it be so for me, O praiser—the impulse is firm—that I should bestow (gifts) on the Soma-presser, the sacrificer. I am the giver without desire for return, the smiter; I crush the mighty one who perverts truth and seeks crookedness.

sanskrit: yadīd ahaṁ yudhaye saṁnayāny adevayūn tanvā śūśujānān | amā te tumraṁ vṛṣabham pacāni tīvraṁ sutam pañcadaśaṁ ni ṣiñcam ||
english: If I were to lead out (my forces) to battle against the Devayū-enemies who had been swelling in body—let me cook a fat bull for thee here at home; let me pour out the potent Soma fifteen times.

sanskrit: nāhaṁ taṁ veda ya iti bravīty adevayūn samaraṇe jaghanvān | yadāvākhyat samaraṇaṁ ṛghāvad ād id dha me vṛṣabhā pra bruvanti ||
english: I do not know him who boasts that he has slain those who do not honour the gods in battle. When my fierce chariot proclaims the battle, then indeed do the bulls speak out in my praise.

sanskrit: yad ajñāteṣu vṛjaneṣu āsaṁ viśve sa to maghavāno ma āsan | jināmi vet kṣema ā santam ābhum pra taṁ kṣiṇām parvate pādagṛhya ||
english: When I was among unknown peoples, all the bountiful ones were on my side. I shall defeat the proud one dwelling in comfort at home—I shall push him from the mountain, having seized him by the foot.

sanskrit: na vā u māṁ vṛjane vārayante na parvatāso yad aham manasye | mama svanāt kṛdhukaro bhayāta eved anu dyūn kiraṇaḥ sam ejāt ||
english: Neither the peoples stop me nor the mountains, when I set my mind (to something). At the sound of my voice the frightened one with the small ears trembles; even so through the days the wren trembles.

sanskrit: darśan nv atra śṛtapāṁ anirndrān bāhukṣadaḥ śarave patyamānān | ghṛṣum vā ye niniduḥ sakhāyam adhy ū nv eṣu pavayo vavṛtyuḥ ||
english: They shall see here those cooked-flesh eaters bereft of Indra, cut off from arms, flying from the arrow—or those who have blamed a bold companion; the wheel-rims shall surely roll over them.

sanskrit: abhūr v aukṣīr vy u āyur ānaḍ darśan nu pūrvo aparo nu darṣat | dve pavaste pari taṁ na bhūto yo asya pāre rajaso viveṣa ||
english: Thou wast born, thou grewest, life came to thee—the former may see (this), the later will see (this). Two wheel-pieces encompass him who has not yet been, who has entered the farther side of this expanse.

sanskrit: gāvo yavam prayutā aryo akṣan tā apaśyaṁ sahagopāś carantīḥ | havā id aryo abhitaḥ sam āyan kiyad āsu svapatiś chandayāte ||
english: The cows of the lord were set loose and ate the barley; I saw them roaming, herded together. The calls of the lord came from all sides to gather them—how many of them will the master of his own house be pleased with?

sanskrit: saṁ yad vayaṁ yavasādo janānām ahaṁ yavāda urvajre antaḥ | atrā yukto 'vasātāram icchād atho ayuktaṁ yunajad vavānvān ||
english: When we, the eaters of barley among peoples—I myself an eater of barley within the broad expanse—here the yoked (one) sought to unyoke, then the unwilling one the eager one harnessed.

sanskrit: atred u me maṁsase satyam uktaṁ dvipāc ca yac catuṣpāt saṁsṛjāni | strībhir yo atra vṛṣaṇam pṛtanyād ayuddho asya vi bhajāni vedaḥ ||
english: And then thou shalt deem my word true—what (wealth) of two-footed and four-footed I shall bring together. If any man here contests with woman the manly one—the unwarlike shall be divided; I know (how to deal with) him.

sanskrit: yasyānakṣā duhitā jātv āsa kas tāṁ vidvāṁ abhi manyāte andhām | kataro meṇim prati tam mucāte ya īṁ vahāte ya īm vā vareyāt ||
english: One whose daughter was born wheelless—who, knowing this, should think lightly of her as blind? Which of the two releases the ram for her—he who would take her away or he who would choose her?

sanskrit: kiyatī yoṣā maryato vadhūyoḥ pariprītā panyasā vāryeṇa | bhadrā vadhūr bhavatī yat supeśāḥ svayaṁ sā mitraṁ vanute jane cit ||
english: How dear is the young woman to the wooing young man when she is well-pleased with the wonderful gift! The bride is auspicious when she is beautiful—she herself wins a friend even among the people.

sanskrit: patto jagāra pratyañcam atti śīrṣṇā śiraḥ prati dadhau varūtham | āsīna ūrdhvām upasi kṣiṇāti nyaṅṅ uttānām anv eti bhūmim ||
english: One awoke from his feet, eats facing forward; with his head he placed a covering against his head. Sitting, he diminishes the lap of the upright one; going downward he follows the supine earth.

sanskrit: bṛhann acchāyo apalāśo arvā tasthau mātā viṣito atti garbhaḥ | anyasyā vatsaṁ rihatī mimāya kayā bhuvā ni dadhe dhenur ūdhaḥ ||
english: A tall (tree) without shade, without leaf, has stood still; the loosened embryo eats the mother. Licking another's calf, she has lowed—where has the cow placed her udder?

sanskrit: sapta vīrāso adharād ud āyann aṣṭottarāttāt sam ajagmiran te | nava paścātāt sthivimanta āyan daśa prāk sānu vi tirany aśnaḥ ||
english: Seven heroes rose up from below; those eight from above came together. Nine mighty ones came from behind; ten from in front spread across the back of the rock.

sanskrit: daśānām ekaṁ kapilaṁ samānaṁ taṁ hinvanti kratave pāryāya | garbham mātā sudhitaṁ vakṣaṇāsv avenantam tuṣayantī bibharti ||
english: One reddish-brown one among ten—the same—they urge him toward the rite for crossing over. The mother carries the well-placed embryo in her womb, soothing him as he turns about.

sanskrit: pīvānam meṣam apacanta vīrā nyuptā akṣā anu dīva āsan | dvā dhanum bṛhatīm apsv antaḥ pavitravantā caratah punantā ||
english: The heroes cooked the fat ram; the dice were cast along the day. Two of them, with purifying strainers, move in the great waters purifying them.

sanskrit: vi krośanāso viṣvañca āyan pacāti nemo na hi pakṣad ardhaḥ | ayam me devaḥ savitā tad āha drvannid vanavat sarpirannnaḥ ||
english: They who were crying out went off in all directions; the half cooks (the share) — the half that does not side (with anyone). This god Savitṛ has told me this: 'He who eats from the wooden vessel will thrive on ghee-food.'

sanskrit: apaśyaṁ grāmaṁ vahamānam ārād acakrayā svadhayā vartamānam | siṣakty arya pra yugā janānāṁ sadyaḥ śiśnā praminaṇo navīyān ||
english: I saw the village being carried away from afar, moving along by its own power without wheels. The lord constantly goes forward through the generations; even now the fresh one, renewing his generative vigour.

sanskrit: etau me gāvau pramarasya yuktau mo ṣu praṣedhīr muhur in mamandhi | āpaś cid asya vi naśanty arthaṁ sūraś ca marka uparo babhūvān ||
english: These two cows of mine are yoked to Pramara—push them not away, make (me) glad again and again! Even the waters lose their power before him; the sun has eclipsed and the hawk has swooped down.

sanskrit: ayaṁ yo vajraḥ purudhā vivṛtto 'vaḥ sūryasya bṛhataḥ purīṣāt | śrava id enā paro anyad asti tad avyathī jarimāṇas taranti ||
english: This vajra that is manifold, unfolded from the great fullness below the sun—beyond that there is yet another renown; the steadfast ones, growing old, cross to that.

sanskrit: vṛkṣe-vṛkṣe niyatā mīmayad gaus tato vayaḥ pra patān pūruṣādaḥ ||  athe idaṁ viśvam bhuvanam bhayāta indrāya sunvad ṛṣaye ca śikṣat ||
english: The cow lows, tied to each tree; thence the man-eating bird shall fly forth. Then let all this world be afraid and let (the reward) be given to the Soma-presser and to the seer (who praises) Indra.

sanskrit: devānām māne prathamā atiṣṭhan kṛntatrād eṣām uparā ud āyan | trayas tapanti pṛthivīm anūpā dvā bṛbūkaṁ vahataḥ purīṣam ||
english: The first (ones) stood at the gods' measure; from that point of cutting the later ones rose up. Three scorch the watery earth; two carry the dung-heap croaking (like frogs).

sanskrit: sā te jīvātur uta tasya viddhi mā smaitādṛg apa gūhaḥ samarye | āviḥ svaḥ kṛṇute gūhate busaṁ sa pādur asya nirṇijo na mucyate ||
english: Know both her life and his—do not hide such a thing as this in battle. He makes the light manifest, he conceals his nakedness; he who has appeared is not freed from his adornment.

sanskrit: viśvo hy anyo arir ājagāma mamed aha śvaśuro nā jagāma | jakṣīyād dhānā uta somam papīyāt svāśitaḥ punar astaṁ jagāyāt ||
english: Any other enemy who comes—but today my father-in-law has not come. Let him eat the grain-cakes and drink the Soma; when well fed let him go home again.

sanskrit: sa roruvad vṛṣabhas tigmaśṛṅgo varṣman tasthau varimanna ā pṛthivyāḥ | viśveṣv enaṁ vṛjaneṣu pāmi yo me kukṣī sutasomaḥ pṛṇāti ||
english: Bellowing, the sharp-horned bull has stood at the top, at the breadth of the earth. I protect him in all the enclosures—him who fills my flanks with pressed Soma.

sanskrit: adriṇā te mandina indra tūyān sunvanti somān pibasi tvam eṣām | pacanti te vṛṣabhāṁ atsi teṣām pṛkṣeṇa yan maghavan hūyamānaḥ ||
english: For thee, O Indra, with the pressing stone they press the exhilarating Soma-draughts quickly; thou drinkest them. They cook bulls for thee; thou eatest from them—thou who art nourished with food when called upon, O bountiful one.

sanskrit: idaṁ su me jaritar ā cikiddhi pratīpaṁ śāpaṁ nadyo vahanti | lopāśaḥ siṁham pratyañcam atsāḥ kroṣṭā varāhaṁ nir atakta kakṣāt ||
english: Understand this well for me, O singer—rivers flow against the current as a curse! The jackal has eaten the lion facing him; the jackal has driven the boar out of the thicket.

sanskrit: kathā ta etad ahaṁ ā ciketaṁ gṛtasya pākas tavaso manīṣām | tvaṁ no vidvāṁ ṛtuthā vi voco yam ardhaṁ te maghavan kṣemyā dhūḥ ||
english: How shall I understand this—the insight of the wise Gṛtsa concerning thy mighty thought? Do thou, knowing (all), speak to us in order—what, O bountiful one, thou drivest as thy pleasant half (of our share).

sanskrit: evā hi māṁ tavasaṁ vardhayanti divaś cin me bṛhata uttarā dhūḥ | purū sahasrā ni śiśāmi sākaṁ aśatruṁ hi mā janitā jajāna ||
english: For thus they increase me, the mighty one—even my higher course is the great (course) of heaven. I smite many thousands simultaneously, for my father begot me without an enemy.

sanskrit: evā hi māṁ tavasaṁ jajñur ugraṁ karman-karma vṛṣaṇam indra devāḥ | vadhīṁ vṛtraṁ vajreṇa mandasāno 'pa vrajaṁ mahinā dāśuṣe vam ||
english: For thus the gods, O Indra, have begotten me—the mighty, the fierce, the manly one at every deed. Exhilarated, I slew Vṛtra with the vajra; I opened the pen (of cows) with my greatness for the worshipper.

sanskrit: devāsa āyan paraśūṁ r a bibhran vanā vṛścanto abhi viḍbhir āyan | ni sudraṁ dadhato vakṣaṇāsu yatrā kṛpītaṁ anu tad dahanti ||
english: The gods came bearing their axes; cutting through forests they came against the enclosed settlements. They place the woodpile upon (the altar's) chest—where the moisture is, they burn along with that.

sanskrit: śaśaḥ kṣuram pratyañcaṁ jagārādriṁ logenam vy abhedam ārāt | bṛhantaṁ cid ṛhate randhayāni vayad vatso vṛṣabhaṁ śūśuvānaḥ ||
english: The hare swallowed the razor point-first; I split the rock from afar with a clod. I shall subdue even the great one for the weak; the calf, striving, weaves (about) the full-grown bull.

sanskrit: suparṇa itthā nakham ā siṣāyāvaruddhaḥ paripadaṁ na siṁhaḥ | niruddhaś cin mahiṣas tarṣyāvān godhā tasmai ayathaṁ karṣad etat ||
english: The eagle thus grips the prey with its talon—checked, like a lion held at the trap. The thirsty buffalo too, though restrained—the lizard has drawn this noose for him.

sanskrit: tebhyo godhā ayathaṁ karṣad etad ye brahmaṇaḥ pratipīyanty annaiḥ | sima ukṣṇo 'vasṛṣṭāṁ adanti svayam balāni tanvaḥ śṛṇānāḥ ||
english: For those who feed on the Brāhmaṇa's food by drinking it against him—the lizard has drawn this snare. They eat the freely-loosed bulls, (yet) sharpening the limbs' own strength.

sanskrit: ete śamībhiḥ śuśamī abhūvan ye hinvire tanvaḥ soma ukthaiḥ | nṛvad vadann upa no māhi vājān divi śravo dadhiṣe nāma vīraḥ ||
english: These have prospered through their labours who urged forward the Soma (for bodily) strength with their hymns. Speak to us in man-like fashion—approach us with prizes! As a hero thou placest thy fame, thy name, in heaven.

sanskrit: vane na vā yo ny adhāyi cākañ śucir vāṁ stomo bhuraṇāv ajīgaḥ | yasyed indraḥ purulineṣu hotā nṛṇāṁ naryo nṛtamaḥ kṣapāvān ||
english: As the fire deposited in the forest resplendent—the pure hymn of praise has been aroused for you two, O sustainers. He for whom Indra, the most manly of men, the heroic one, the night-passing Hotṛ among many lineages—

sanskrit: pra te asyā uṣasaḥ prāparasyā nṛtau syāma nṛtamasya nṛṇām | anu triśokaḥ śatam āvahan nṛn kutsena ratho yo asat sasavān ||
english: Beyond this dawn and the next may we be in the manliness of the most manly among men. Triśoka drove a hundred men after (the battle)—the chariot that (aided) Kutsa achieved victory.

sanskrit: kas te mada indra rantyo bhūd duro giro abhy ugro vi dhāva | kad vāho arvāg upa mā manīṣā ā tvā śakyām upamaṁ rādho annaiḥ ||
english: Which of thy pleasurable exhilarations has arisen, O Indra? Rush forth, fierce one, against the doors (of thy strongholds) with (our) hymns! What oblation may bring thee close to us? May I be able to approach thee with food to (offer) the highest gift.

sanskrit: kad u dyumnam indra tvāvato nṝn kayā dhiyā karase kan na āgan | mitro na satya urugāya bṛtyā anne samasya yad asan manīṣāḥ ||
english: What splendour dost thou, O Indra, make for such men? By what thought dost thou come to us? Like Mitra, true and far-striding, in the presence of food, of all (the foods)—as the inspired prayers shall be.

sanskrit: preraya sūro arthaṁ na pāraṁ ye asya kāmaṁ janidhā iva gman | giraś ca ye te tuvijāta pūrvīr nara indra pratiśikṣanty annaiḥ ||
english: The sun urges (them) to the goal, like (a boat) to the farther shore—those who have gone like mothers (come) to his desire. And the many hymns addressed to thee, O Indra nobly born—men who praise thee receive (their reward) with foods.

sanskrit: mātre nu te sumite indra pūrvī dyaur majmanā pṛthivī kāvyena | varāya te ghṛtavantaḥ sutāsaḥ svādman bhavantu pītaye madhūni ||
english: Immense indeed for thy mother, O Indra, are heaven by grandeur and earth by wisdom. For thy choice, may the ghee-mixed Soma-pressings be sweet for thee to drink—the honied draughts.

sanskrit: ā madhvo asmā asicannam atraṁ indrāya pūrṇaṁ sa hi satyarādhāḥ | sa vāvṛdhe varimanna ā pṛthivyā abhi kratvā narya pauṁsyaiś ca ||
english: They poured out for him the vessel full of sweet Soma—for Indra, for he is the truly bountiful. He has grown great in the breadth of the earth, in his will, in manly power and virility.

sanskrit: vy ānaḍ indraḥ pṛtanāḥ svojā āsmai yatante sakhyāya pūrvīḥ ||  ā smā rathaṁ na pṛtanāsu tiṣṭha yam bhadrayā sumatyā codayāse ||
english: Indra has spread out the battle-hosts with his own might; many (allies) endeavour for friendship with him. Stand firm in the battles as on a chariot—him whom thou urgest on with (thy) auspicious benevolence.

sanskrit: pra devatrā brahmaṇe gātur etv apo acchā manaso na prayukti | mahīm mitrasya varuṇasya dhāsim pṛthujrayase rīradhā suvṛktim ||
english: Let the path go forth to the gods for the Brahman priest, toward the waters—like the impulse of the mind. Render up the great sustenance of Mitra and Varuṇa in beautifully constructed prayer to the far-spreading one.

sanskrit: adhvaryavo haviṣmanto hi bhūtācchāpa itośatīr uśantaḥ | ava yāś caṣṭe aruṇaḥ suparṇas tam āsyadhvam ūrmim adyā suhastāḥ ||
english: O Adhvaryus bearing oblations—eager ones approaching the invoked (Waters), eager (themselves)—what the red eagle beholds descending—draw that wave to yourselves today, O dexterous ones.

sanskrit: adhvaryavo 'pa itā samudram apāṁ napātaṁ haviṣā yajadhvam | sa vo dadad ūrmim adyā supūtaṁ tasmai somam madhumantaṁ sunota ||
english: O Adhvaryus, go toward the ocean; worship Apāṁ Napāt (Child of the Waters) with your oblation. He will give you today a pure wave—press for him the honey-sweet Soma.

sanskrit: yo aniddhmo dīdayad apsv antar yaṁ viprāsa īḻate adhvareṣu | apāṁ napān madhumatīr apo dā yābhir indro vāvṛdhe vīryāya ||
english: He who shines without fuel within the waters—whom the inspired priests praise at the rites—O Apāṁ Napāt, give the honey-sweet waters by which Indra has grown to might.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ somo modate harṣate ca kalyāṇībhir yuvatibhir na maryaḥ | tā adhvaryo apo acchā parehi yad āsiñcā oṣadhībhiḥ punītāt ||
english: O Adhvaryu, go toward those waters by which Soma is pleased and exhilarated, like a young man (pleased) with beautiful maidens. May the water purify what thou shalt have poured in, together with the herbs.

sanskrit: eved yūne yuvatayo namanta yad īm uśann uśatīr ety accha | saṁ jānate manasā saṁ cikirtre 'dhvaryavo dhiṣaṇāpaś ca devīḥ ||
english: Thus indeed do the young women bow to the young man, when the eager one comes to the eager ones. They understand one another with mind, they have discerned (each other)—the Adhvaryus and the divine Dhiṣaṇā-waters.

sanskrit: yo vo vṛtābhyo akṛṇod u lokaṁ yo vo mahyā abhiśaster amuñcat | tasmā indrāya madhumantam ūrmiṁ devamādanam pra hiṇotanāpaḥ ||
english: For him who made a world-space out of your enclosures, who freed you from the great curse—for him, for Indra, send forward the honey-sweet wave, the god-exhilarating one, O Waters.

sanskrit: prāsmai hinota madhumantam ūrmiṁ garbho yo vaḥ sindhavo madhva utsa ḥ | ghṛtapṛṣṭham īḍyam adhvareṣv āpo revatīḥ śṛṇutā havam me ||
english: Send forward for him the honey-sweet wave—the embryo who is the spring of sweetness for you, O rivers. O rich Waters, praised at the rites with ghee-backed offerings—hear my call.

sanskrit: taṁ sindhavo matsaram indrapānam ūrmim pra heta ya ubhe iyarti | madacyutam auśānaṁ nabhojām pari tritantum vicaṁ rantam utsam ||
english: O rivers, send that exhilarating wave fit for Indra's drinking—him who stirs both (worlds). (Send) the intoxication-shedding, Uśanā-born, cloud-born one circling around the three-threaded, mobile spring.

sanskrit: āvarvṛtatīr adha nu dvidhārā goṣuyudho na niyavaṁ carantīḥ | ṛṣe janitrīr bhuvanasya patnīr apo vandasva savṛdhaḥ sayonīḥ ||
english: Rolling onward in two streams, now fighting over the cattle like warriors heading for the stall—O seer, revere the waters, the mothers and mistresses of the world, those who increase together, those who share the same womb.

sanskrit: hinnotā no adhvaraṁ devayajyā hinota brahma sanaye dhanānām | ṛtasya yoge vi ṣyadhvam ūdhaḥ śruṣṭīvarīr bhūtanāsmabhyam āpaḥ ||
english: Help our rite with your divine worship; help the sacred prayer for winning of wealth. At the yoking of ṛta release your udder—O Waters, be quick-hearing, attentive to us.

sanskrit: āpo revatīḥ kṣayathā hi vasva ḥ kratuṁ ca bhadram bibhṛthāmṛtaṁ ca | rāyaś ca stha svapatasya patnīḥ sarasvatī tad gṛṇate vayo dhāt ||
english: O rich Waters, you dwell on riches; you bear the auspicious will and immortality. You are the wives of him whose offspring is excellent—may Sarasvatī grant strength to him who praises this.

sanskrit: prati yad āpo adṛśram āyatīr ghṛtam payāṁsi bibhratīr madhūni | adhvaryubhir manasā saṁvidānā indrāya somaṁ suṣutam bharantīḥ ||
english: When the Waters were seen coming, bearing ghee, milks, and honey, agreeing with the Adhvaryus in mind—bringing the well-pressed Soma for Indra—

sanskrit: emā agman revatīr jīvadhanā adhvaryavaḥ sādayatā sakhāyaḥ ||  ni barhiṣi dhattana somyāso 'pāṁ naptrā saṁvidānāsā enāḥ ||
english: These rich Waters bringing living riches have come. O Adhvaryus, friends, make them sit down! Seat these Soma-bearing ones on the sacred grass, in agreement with Apāṁ Napāt.

sanskrit: āgmann āpa uśatīr barhir edaṁ ny adhvare asadan devayantīḥ | adhvaryavaḥ sunu tendrāya somaṁ abhūd u vaḥ śuśakā devayajyā ||
english: The eager Waters have come; they have sat down here on the sacred grass at the rite, seeking the gods. O Adhvaryus, press the Soma for Indra—your divine worship has become efficacious.
